title: Hierarchical & Grouped Forecast Reconciliation
interviewAnswer: When forecasts exist at product, region and total levels, independently trained models can be incoherent. Reconciliation adjusts forecasts so aggregation constraints are satisfied while preserving accuracy as much as possible.
keyPoints: Bottom-up, top-down and optimal reconciliation differ.
Hierarchy can be crossed/grouped, not only a tree.
Accuracy should be assessed across levels.
why: Hierarchical & Grouped Forecast Reconciliation appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: Bottom-up, top-down and optimal reconciliation differ.
deepDive: When forecasts exist at product, region and total levels, independently trained models can be incoherent. Reconciliation adjusts forecasts so aggregation constraints are satisfied while preserving accuracy as much as possible. Hierarchy can be crossed/grouped, not only a tree. Accuracy should be assessed across levels. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Product forecasts should sum to category and company forecasts after reconciliation.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Hierarchical & Grouped Forecast Reconciliation make?
How would you validate or debug Hierarchical & Grouped Forecast Reconciliation in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
